notes:
Summary: mid-market workflow automation vendor targeting customer support and operational automation. Evaluating Redwood Hosted API as low-friction POC; likely Dedicated if latency and tool reliability SLA requirements met.

Timeline / recent activity:
- 2025-11-02: inbound lead from webinar; basic qualification by Maya.
- 2025-12-08: discovery call (Maya + Daniel) — use-case: agentic customer support bot + automation for field ops.
- 2026-01-20: demo of Hosted API (streaming + tool calling) — showed basic search+action flow.
- 2026-02-10: POC kickoff (2-week sandbox) — integration with internal search, ticketing system (custom tool).
- 2026-02-25: POC mid-review — initial latencies good but intermittent tool-call failures observed.
- 2026-03-02: POC results review (fireflies ff_20260302_poc_review) — saw ~8% tool-call error rate during spike; 90th percentile token latency for streaming ~220ms, median ~80ms.
- 2026-03-09: pricing + architecture sync with infra and security teams.

Technical requirements / notes:
- Workload: agentic multi-step flows (search -> plan -> tool-call(s) -> confirm). High concurrency expected during peak (80-120 concurrent agent sessions).
- Latency SLO: target tail latency <=200ms for streaming token delivery; desire sub-150ms median. Client product managers: "If streaming lags, users drop out".
- Tool calling: must support reliable tool-call orchestration with idempotency and clear timeout semantics. Current POC saw timeouts inside their tool chain (custom ticketing API) causing partial failures and poor UX.
- Fallbacks: want model routing + automatic fallback to smaller variant or cached answer for degraded tool-call availability.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-market; acceptable ARR band but expect predictable monthly committed spend if Dedicated.
- Security: SSO/SAML, SOC2 attestation, audit logs for model inputs/outputs, KMS integration for keys. EU data residency required for a subset of customers.

POC findings & feedback:
- Hosted API got them 80% of the way for feature validation: easy streaming and tool-call prototyping.
- Observed failure modes: orchestration timeouts (downstream ticket API), transient kernel OOM on long-context queries (rare), backpressure handling during bursts was inconsistent.
- They liked Redwood's auto-batching and KV cache ideas for reducing token costs — asked for batching controls per-route.
- Requested clear SLA pricing for Dedicated with a burst cushion and runbook for multi-step tool failures.

Quotes / call snippets:
- VP Product (Ana Morales): "We need the assistant to finish actions reliably — a 5-10% failure rate on tool actions is a showstopper."
- Engineering lead (Tom Bates): "If you can guarantee tail latency and give us deterministic timeouts for tool calls we can consider moving to Dedicated."

Next steps / action items:
- SE (Daniel) to run focused stress test on tool-calling orchestration against their staging ticket API to reproduce and surface exact failure points (target: 3/16).
- Maya to coordinate pricing call with finance (provide Dedicated baseline + burst SLA options) week of 3/16.
- Security to provide SOC2 + KMS integration notes; legal to confirm EU data residency options.
- CSM (Rita) to prepare onboarding checklist and 30/60/90 success milestones if they convert.
